newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares slip at noon in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares slip at noon in dull trading.

text.p: Shanghai B shares slipped at midday on Monday in dull trading with few buying orders making if difficult for overseas investors to continue their liquidation, brokers said.
The index fell 0.264 points or 0.56 percent to 46.917 points on volume of 945,000 shares worth $381,000. Of 41 B shares, only 19 traded with nine down, nine flat and one up.
Brokers said market sentiment was very weak with few buying orders, and the index could test a new low in the afternoon.
"Poor market sentiment have made most shares less tradable," one broker said.
"More overseas liquidation is expected in the afternoon, which will push the index to a record low," a second broker predicted.
Shanghai Industrial Sewing Machine traded most and lost most on unwinding selling, plunging $0.020 or 16.66 percent to $0.100 on volume of 264,000 shares.
Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development traded the second most on institutional selling, falling $0.008 or 0.90 percent to $0.872 on volume of 255,600 shares.
Shanghai A shares were up on a technical rebound after plunges in the past few days, but most investors remained cautious about following up, brokers said.
The A index gained 5.365 points or 0.55 percent to 984.535 points on volume of 163.3 million shares worth 1.6 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index rose 11.265 or 0.46 percent to 2471.259 points.
Sichuan International was the star on speculative buying, soaring 0.90 yuan or 12.32 percent to 8.20 yuan on volume of 954,400 shares.
